Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise plan and the artifacts we'll provide by Feb 17 PST so you can include them in the SIG packet.

Summary attestation (draft):
Redwood Inference maintains a documented vulnerability management program that includes authenticated weekly scans of production images, a monthly credentialed full infrastructure scan, and a quarterly third-party penetration test. We commit to remediation SLAs measured from confirmed reproducible findings as follows: Critical (CVSS 9.0-10.0): 7 calendar days; High (7.0-8.9): 30 calendar days; Medium (4.0-6.9): 90 calendar days. Ownership for triage and remediation is delegated to platform teams with explicit ticketing and escalation paths. Where applicable, compensating controls are documented. (Signed attestation PDF and evidence bundle attached.)

Planned evidence bundle (attached in next email):
- scan-snapshot-20260210.csv — last 3 scheduled scan runs and sample findings
- cve-ownership-matrix-20260215.xlsx — mapping: infra (Karthik Iyer), serving runtime (Marissa Cole), infra-as-code (Laura Bennett) plus escalation contact info
- remediation-attestation-signed-20260217.pdf — final signed statement (will send once signed)

A couple of clarifications:
- SLA timing starts from the time the issue is confirmed reproducible in our triage flow (not from raw scan noise).
- Exceptions are documented for third-party components where vendor patches are required; those are tracked in our VM board (VM-7891).

Internal owners:
- Karthik Iyer — platform/infrastructure remediation lead (owner: VM-7891, VM-7934)
- Marissa Cole — runtime/model serving remediation (owner: VM-8002)
- Laura Bennett — IaC and deployment pipelines (owner: VM-7950)

We will attach the CSV and ownership matrix in the follow-up and Marissa will append the signed attestation. Reach out if you need alternate formatting (table, single-page summary, or DocuSign).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Security Operations
